name: Cervélo Áspero-5
why_interesting: An explicitly aerodynamic gravel-race platform with up to 45 mm clearance, a 1,023 g reported frame and current complete-build options.
missing: Current mainland seller, selected checkout price, stock and warranty route
Current manufacturer frameset weight with full size, paint and hardware basis
Public test protocol behind the manufacturer's current aerodynamic claims
price_status: official global price converted to CNY; mainland checkout unverified

official_price.price_basis: Current official frameset price; excludes actual FX, shipping, tax and duties

facts.frame: Cervélo Áspero-5 aerodynamic gravel-race carbon frameset
facts.frame_material: Carbon frame and fork; exact fiber supplier, grades and lay-up are not published
facts.frame_construction: S5-influenced aerodynamic shaping, internal storage, threaded bottom bracket and UDH
facts.stiffness_evidence: The manufacturer publishes aerodynamic savings but no public stiffness value; one independent review noted cockpit flex rather than frame deflection
facts.frame_weight_basis: BikeRadar reports Cervélo's 1,023 g frame and 393 g fork figures for the current generation; size, paint and included hardware are not stated
facts.tire_clearance_basis: Official maximum. Cervélo recommends 42/42 mm for balance or 40 mm front / 44 mm rear for a more aerodynamic setup

alternative_builds.label: Official GRX RX827 Di2 build

price.price_basis: Current official USD 8,850 complete-bike price converted at the dated central-parity reference

alternative_builds.notes: Official current build; a mainland selected-option price was not found in this pass.

alternative_builds.label: BikeRadar size-58 test bike
alternative_builds.weight_basis: Independent complete test-bike measurement around 8.26 kg in size 58
alternative_builds.notes: Independent current-generation test configuration; its weight is not combined with the official GRX price.

source_note: This model is kept in the new wide-clearance aero category because Cervélo explicitly designs it around aerodynamic gravel racing. Its gravel discipline remains visible in the title and notes rather than being relabeled as a conventional road bike.
